Apple's developer blog today announced tax and pricing updates for apps, in-app purchases, and subscriptions in multiple regions. Details are as follows.

Three countries implement tax changes starting today

Apple published a new article on its developer blog, announcing two rounds of tax and pricing adjustments for apps and in-app purchases across multiple App Store storefronts.

The first round takes effect today, adjusting developer proceeds to reflect new or updated taxes in three countries:

Morocco: Introduction of 20% Value Added Tax (VAT) Republic of the Congo: Introduction of 18% Value Added Tax (VAT) Tanzania: Digital Services Tax (DST) rate increased from 2% to 3%

The second round takes effect on September 14, adjusting App Store pricing in four countries. The article states as follows:

If you have not set Israel, Indonesia, Morocco, or the Republic of the Congo as the base storefront for your app or in-app purchases, pricing for apps and in-app purchases in those regions will be updated. These adjustments also take into account the VAT introductions mentioned in the tax updates section above. If you have set Israel, Indonesia, Morocco, or the Republic of the Congo as the base storefront for your app or in-app purchases, pricing in that storefront will not change. Pricing in other storefronts will be updated to keep your selected base price aligned.

Although Apple did not provide details on the specific pricing changes in its announcement, the company said the new prices are available for review in the "Pricing and Availability" section of App Store Connect.

Apple further noted, "If an in-app purchase is an auto-renewable subscription, prices won't change in any region," and the same applies to storefronts where prices are managed manually by developers rather than using the company's automatic pricing equalization.

The company said these adjustments are part of its routine procedures to reflect changes in tax regulations and foreign exchange rates.
